requirement: Sign and verify large streamed payloads with RSA-PSS over SHA-256 without buffering them, interoperating with standard PSS signatures and treating any bad signature as a False result.
skeleton: A PSS padding factory with a fixed salt, an incremental SHA-256 digest helper, sign_stream checking the key size and signing prehashed, and verify_stream checking length and catching InvalidSignature.
caption: Detached RSA-PSS signatures over streamed data with the cryptography library. _pss builds padding.PSS with MGF1 over hashes.SHA256 and a fixed salt_length of SALT_BYTES, 32. _digest feeds every chunk into hashes.Hash(SHA256) and returns finalize, so the chunking never changes the result. sign_stream(private, chunks) raises ValueError saying the RSA key must be at least 2048 bits, then signs the digest with PSS and utils.Prehashed(hashes.SHA256()), which equals signing the whole stream. verify_stream(public, chunks, signature) returns False for a signature that is not key_size // 8 bytes, verifies the prehashed digest the same way, and returns False on InvalidSignature, True otherwise. The fixture asserts that a signature over 1000 byte chunks is 256 bytes and verifies with its own PSS salt 32 over the whole data, that a one-chunk signature verifies against 7 byte chunks, that a reference signature verifies, that tampered data, another key, a truncated signature and an all-zero signature return False, and that a 1024 bit key raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Sign release artifacts too large to hold in memory
constraints: Signatures are RSA-PSS with MGF1-SHA256 and a 32 byte salt
The stream is hashed incrementally and signed with Prehashed SHA-256
Chunk boundaries never affect the signature
Wrong length, tampered or foreign signatures return False instead of raising InvalidSignature

rationale.teaches: Hash the stream incrementally, sign with utils.Prehashed so the result matches a one-shot PSS signature, and fix the salt length on both sides.
rationale.why: PKCS1v15, a different salt length or double hashing all produce signatures that only the same buggy code can verify.

ops.docstring: Detached RSA-PSS signatures over streamed data.

ops.stmt: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding, rsa, utils

candidates.why_wrong: Signing uses PKCS1v15 padding, so PSS verifiers reject every signature.
The salt is 20 bytes, so signatures do not match the 32 byte PSS profile.
1024 bit keys are accepted for signing.
A bad signature of the right length raises InvalidSignature instead of returning False.
Verification hashes the digest again, so no valid signature ever verifies.
